title: Building Credibility Quickly in a New Role
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece addresses a tension new leaders face: conventional advice says to listen first and avoid rushing into big changes, but that caution alone can leave a leader looking passive. The essay argues the missing ingredient is quick, low-risk wins — small, visible improvements to existing processes that don't require a change in strategy or personnel. These 'low-hanging fruit' fixes build credibility while a listening tour is still underway, buying the new leader room to make bigger, harder changes later once they've earned trust. The piece frames this as a parallel-track approach: listen deeply for the big decisions, but act immediately on small ones.
points: New leaders are commonly told to listen first, but that advice alone can look like inaction.
Small, visible wins on existing processes build credibility fast without requiring big strategic bets.
Low-hanging-fruit fixes don't interfere with the need to first listen to the team before making bigger changes.
Demonstrating competence on small matters buys leaders room to eventually pursue heavier changes.
The best new leaders run both tracks at once — listening deeply while acting quickly on what's easy to fix.
quotes: Leaders instinctively know that establishing their credibility quickly with the team is critical to their short- and long-term success.
To build credibility with the team, they must also score some quick wins, making the team instantly more effective.
This so-called “low-hanging fruit” typically does not involve significant change but instead invites a tweak or small correction to an existing process or approach.
Small improvements become big signs that a new leader is credible.
The best new leaders look for where they can make a difference quickly and focus their attention on improvements that everyone will view positively.
